stats_chi2_specified.description: Find expected counts, pool small classes and run a chi-squared goodness-of-fit test for a specified discrete model.

sections.title: How do probabilities become expected counts?
sections.label: Expected counts
sections.intro: The expected total equals the observed total because all possible outcomes are accounted for.

blocks.html: Multiply each model probability by the sample size. A fractional expected count is entirely possible.
Replacing a fractional expected count with the nearest integer can change the statistic.

blocks.title: Find the expected Blue count
blocks.prompt:
An independent sample of colour cards is compared with the producer’s proportions. Under the proposed model the class probabilities in order are \(\frac{3}{10},\ \frac{1}{5},\ \frac{1}{10},\ \frac{2}{5}\).

CategoryObserved
Amber\(18\)
Blue\(22\)
Coral\(14\)
Denim\(6\)

Find the expected frequency for Blue. Give an exact value.
blocks.hint: Find each expected count from the model. Use the final classes to count degrees of freedom.
blocks.solution:
\(E_i=60\mathrm{P}(X\text{ is in class }i)\)

Final classObservedExpectedContribution
Amber\(18\)\(18\)\(0\)
Blue\(22\)\(12\)\(\frac{25}{3}\)
Coral\(14\)\(6\)\(\frac{32}{3}\)
Denim\(6\)\(24\)\(\frac{27}{2}\)

The statistic is \(\frac{65}{2}\) with \(\nu=4-1-0=3\) degrees of freedom. The 5% upper critical value is \(7.815\).

There is evidence against the claim that the producer’s model gives the colour proportions.

Method in one minute

Use unrounded expected frequencies in every contribution.

StepWhat to write
Count\(E_i=n p_i\)
PoolAdd both counts before evaluating \(X^2=\sum_i\frac{(O_i-E_i)^2}{E_i}\)

revision.checks:
• Expected count at least 5 in every final class or cell.
  • The critical region is in the upper tail.
  • State your conclusion in context.
revision.examTip: Use the significance level and degrees of freedom together. Failing to reject does not establish the null hypothesis.

stats_chi2_estimated.description: Estimate binomial or Poisson parameters from the sample and use the correct degrees of freedom for chi-squared tests.

sections.title: What information estimates the model?
sections.label: Estimate
sections.intro: Work with the full data before pooling any classes.

blocks.html: For \(X\sim\mathrm{Bin}(m,p)\) use \(\widehat p=\frac{\bar x}{m}\). For a Poisson count use \(\widehat\lambda=\bar x\).
The sample mean of the binomial count can exceed 1. Divide it by the number of trials to estimate the success probability.
